title: PV Diagrams & Cyclic Processes
theory: Net work per cycle = **enclosed area**: positive if the cycle runs **clockwise** on standard P–V axes, negative if counter-clockwise. Over a full cycle $\Delta U = 0$, so $Q_{net} = W_{net}$. Thermal efficiency $\eta = \dfrac{W_{net}}{Q_{in}}$, where $Q_{in}$ sums **only the heat-absorbing legs** (exhaust legs are not "negative input"). Rectangle cycles have only isobaric/isochoric legs — pure $\Delta(PV)$ arithmetic via Topic 21.
framework: Tabulate $(P, V)$ — and hence $PV \propto T$ — at the corners.
Sanity: the Q column must sum to the signed area.

parts.title: Temperature ratio T_A : T_C
parts.parameters:
- Given: 1 mol monatomic ideal gas; A$(V_0, p_0)$ → B$(3V_0, p_0)$ → C$(3V_0, 4p_0)$ → D$(V_0, 4p_0)$ → A. (Right along the bottom, up, left along the top, down: **counter-clockwise**.)
- Find: $T_A/T_C$; work on A→B; the leg of maximum heat absorption and its value; net heat exchanged per cycle.
- Diagram: rectangle of width $2V_0$, height $3p_0$ on P–V axes.

parts.title: Net heat over one full cycle
parts.parameters:
- Given: 1 mol monatomic ideal gas; A$(V_0, p_0)$ → B$(3V_0, p_0)$ → C$(3V_0, 4p_0)$ → D$(V_0, 4p_0)$ → A. (Right along the bottom, up, left along the top, down: **counter-clockwise**.)
- Find: $T_A/T_C$; work on A→B; the leg of maximum heat absorption and its value; net heat exchanged per cycle.
- Diagram: rectangle of width $2V_0$, height $3p_0$ on P–V axes.
parts.calculations: area $= (2V_0)(3p_0) = 6p_0V_0$ ⇒ $W_{net} = -6p_0V_0$ ⇒ the gas **emits** $6p_0V_0$. Check by summing the legs: $5 + \frac{27}{2} - 20 - \frac{9}{2} = -6$ ✓.
parts.conclusion: a CCW cycle is refrigerator-like: net work done **on** the gas, net heat **out**. Reading the arrow direction on the figure is worth two of the five marks here — circle it before computing anything.

parts.title: Heat absorbed A→B (isochoric)
parts.parameters:
- Given: 1 mol monatomic gas ($C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$); A$(V_0, P_0)$ →isochoric→ B$(V_0, 4P_0)$ →isobaric→ C$(4V_0, 4P_0)$ →isochoric→ D$(4V_0, P_0)$ →isobaric→ A. **Clockwise.**
- Find: $Q_{AB}$; $Q_{BC}$; net work per cycle; thermal efficiency.

parts.title: Thermal efficiency
parts.parameters:
- Given: 1 mol monatomic gas ($C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$); A$(V_0, P_0)$ →isochoric→ B$(V_0, 4P_0)$ →isobaric→ C$(4V_0, 4P_0)$ →isochoric→ D$(4V_0, P_0)$ →isobaric→ A. **Clockwise.**
- Find: $Q_{AB}$; $Q_{BC}$; net work per cycle; thermal efficiency.
parts.formulas: $\eta = \dfrac{W_{net}}{Q_{in}}$, with $Q_{in}$ = positive-Q legs only (AB and BC here; CD and DA reject heat).
parts.conclusion: $\eta \approx 26\%$, well below the Carnot bound between the same temperature extremes ($T_C = 16\,T_A$ ⇒ Carnot $= 15/16$) — a sanity reflex worth running every time. The #1 error is subtracting the exhaust legs inside $Q_{in}$: exhaust is exhaust, not negative input.
